utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I would like to briefly deal with a few matters, procedural matters. The first is that the registry has informally given notice to the Trial Chamber that none of the witnesses subpoenaed for the 25th or the 26th of June - and I'm talking about Witnesses with the number 10; Witness with number 48 in the tentative order of testimony; and Witness 30 - that none of them has presented himself at the premises of the Tribunal. The next matter is the Defence would indicate which exhibits used during the testimony of Bogdan Tomas would be tendered, and perhaps we could -- the Defence could refer to the tabs in the yellow binder so that Madam Registrar is able to assign numbers to the extent not yet done, prepare it so that a further -- further submissions on admission of these exhibits can take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can I go through them in order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Number 1 is already exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Numbers 2 to 11 are tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar informs me, Mr. Emmerson, that 2 is also exhibited already, so that would then make 3 to 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any others?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then number 12 is already exhibited, it's an extract from D85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 13 is not tendered at this stage. That witness is due to be called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 14 has in a redacted form been tendered in the context of the evidence of the witnesses currently in the witness box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I wondered, I think that that's perhaps a matter to be discussed, that is, if we have an unredacted copy of a statement tendered and admitted into evidence, whether the public version which gives less and adds nothing at all, but only makes clear that -- for the public that this document or at least the totality of the document is in evidence, whether we should admit that for --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- for evidentiary purposes there's no reason for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In this context I think there may be in the sense that this is not a redacted document where the redactions exist in order to preserve confidentiality. This is a document that was redacted because the Trial Chamber excluded portions of that witness's 92 ter statement from admission to the record and that was done subsequent to the inclusion of the unredacted version in this bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that -- in fact, none of the passages upon which I cross-examined are passages which have since been redacted. So I think the sensible course would be for tab 14 to be substituted with the redacted version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But in any event, it's -- it is a -- it is already an admitted document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab 15 is awaiting the evidence of the witness who is to come next. Tab 16 was not the subject of cross-examination, but is likely to be the subject of cross-examination with either the current witness or the witness to follow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can wait until -- unless Your Honour wishes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. If that would be the case, you can tender that when this material is used.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And tab 17, likewise, is not tendered at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear. Madam Registrar will prepare a list, will assign numbers, and once she has done that we can deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As I stand here, I'm conscious of the fact that there may be two other exhibits between 3 and 11 which have already been assigned exhibit numbers during the evidence in chief of Mr. Tomas and I will, if I may, cross-check that with Madam Registrar in the next break to ensure that they have same documents which require some different assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least it's clear what the Defence would like to have in evidence and then please verify with Madam Registrar what is already in evidence. Then my next question is: Is the -- the 92 ter statement, the redacted statement of the present witness, that is, P377 where certain parts have been excluded, is a hard copy with the redactions available and has it been uploaded in the system?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it has been provided to the registry to be uploaded into e-court, and I believe there is a hard copy available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we don't need seven or eight hard copies, but at least just one hard copy just to verify whether it -- whether the redactions are in line with the decision of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, is there any objection against admission of the redacted P377 and the photos, that's P378. I see no objections, therefore P377 and P378 are admitted into evidence. The Chamber is aware that you, Ms. Issa, you'd like to have some additional time for the examination-in-chief of the present witness. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there was some time taken up with the submissions yesterday as well as the numerous objections, and I'm hoping to stream-line it as much as I possibly can, and I would ask for a bit more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the next issue, the Chamber has been informed -- the Chamber has been informed that there's an issue -- a disclosure issue, a disclosure issue in relation to a statement taken on the 4th of January of this year, a statement from Mr. Musaj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue with that. Disclosure, Mr. Re, has now taken place under what rule?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Rule 66.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Rule 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yeah. It's a statement the OTP had of Mr. Ljulj Musaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of the 14th -- sorry, the 4th of January, earlier this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In terms of the reason for disclosure today, the only thing I can say is that it was just overlooked during the disclosure process. It was found during a search, which is ongoing, under the words "Lake Radonjic"." We do a lot of different searches -- searches under different terms, witness names, KLA terms, and we're doing one under Lake Radonjic and this came up. Now, of course, this should have been disclosed earlier under Rule 66B. And I apologise for that oversight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: However, I make quite clear having viewed the statement that the Defence cross-examined the witness on, the Defence statement and the Prosecution statement, there is virtually no difference in substance. In fact, the Prosecution statement mentions the fact that the witness had -- or Mr. Musaj had spoken to two English people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, if I can stop you there. I do understand that you concede it should have been disclosed earlier. And now you start explaining to us about the content. Isn't it for the Chamber itself to deal with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, of course it is, but I anticipated the Defence are about to tell you about the prejudice they might have suffered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the before we start talking about it, why has the Chamber not received a copy from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why haven't we given you a copy of the statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, why haven't you disclosed it to the Chamber and only to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can't answer that. I do apologise. We should have given it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under Rule 67(C). "If either party discovers additional evidence or material which should have been disclosed earlier pursuant to the Rules, that party shall immediately disclose that evidence or material to the other party and the Trial Chamber." Before we have any further discussions on the matter, the Chamber would insist on compliance with Rule 67(C).

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We will get it to the Trial Chamber immediately, and again I apologise for overlooking the provisions of Rule 67(C).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. The Chamber would rather not discuss it any further at this moment until it has seen that material. Then the Chamber was informed that as far as scheduling next week is concerned, that the parties would meet and see whether they could resolve the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Certain matters have been resolved --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- as I understand it. So far as the next witness is concerned, if we reach the point today when that witness is to start his evidence in chief, which I think may be an open question, but if we do then, as we indicated to the Trial Chamber yesterday afternoon, Mr. Dutertre has been kind enough to waive strict compliance with the Trial Chamber's order for disclosure at the time that the witness is sworn in and the materials to be used in cross-examination. And so it's likely that that witness will take up a significant portion of the day on Monday. I think the Trial Chamber has been copied in on an exchange of correspondence so far as the two Prosecution pathologists are concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, just to put that on the record there was some debate about whether there had been an oral announcement of these two experts to be called next week. Parties disagree on these facts. The Chamber is not very much inclined at this moment to further explore those facts but just establishes that there was disagreement on that. And the Defence has explained its difficulties to cross-examine those experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The position is this, that there have been discussions. The Defence have put forward by e-mail and face-to-face two alternative proposals. One is to adjourn the evidence of both witnesses until a later stage and the other is to hear their evidence in chief and have them recalled at a later stage, and I think the Prosecution are currently considering those suggestions and hopefully will be in a position to respond to them later in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Chamber will wait and see what the response or hear what the response of the Prosecution will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson has outlined correctly. We are considering and trying to jiggle things around a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In relation to the Rule 67(C) matter you raised a moment ago, if Your Honours require submissions on it today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No submissions, the Chamber -- I think that's the gist of Rule 67(C) that if there's late disclosure that by disclosing the material to the Chamber, the Chamber can form a provisional opinion on what that material is, what the impact might be, and it may invite the parties for further submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I understand. All I was asking was I wish to leave my colleagues to tend to this witness, and if my presence is required a message can be sent to me. That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not at this moment. If you start copying this 4th of January statement, Mr. Re, and send it to the Chamber, that would be appreciated. Then we'll hear later this afternoon, we'll hear from the Prosecution what their position will be in relation to the witnesses to be called next week. Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one other matter. Can I inquire whether the Trial Chamber have been provided with a copy of an e-mail from the Defence to the Prosecution identifying certain paragraphs in the 92 ter statement of the next witness to which objection is taken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact if that is the e-mail -- I think we -- let me just check. If that's the one of 12.41 p.m. of today, sent by Mr. Dixon to Mr. Re, that has been forwarded meanwhile to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very much obliged. That will give the Chamber an opportunity to consider those paragraphs at some point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least we can read them and prepare ourselves for further submissions on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just on that matter, I did copy an e-mail to the Chambers on this very matter. We would explicitly asked that this be done in writing, and I'm grateful they have done it this time before the witness takes the stand and so we can resolve it and the time is not taken from our examination-in-chief time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I do understand from what I remember that Mr. Emmerson responded that he took your point and that he apologised for not having done it. So therefore the Chamber was delighted to see that that finally had been settled.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally this: We have today filed a motion for the exclusion of certain portions of the evidence of the next witness, and that is obviously a matter which at some point Your Honours will want to consider and perhaps give directions upon, but it may be that if we reach the position where the next witness is called some preliminary directions will need to be given as to how to handle that part of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand that. I'm looking forward to the next break so that I can read it. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I had a brief conversation today with Mr. Dutertre concerning any objections or suggestions we might have with regard to the next 92 ter. I informed that I would be getting them to him this afternoon. We're trying to coordinate to make sure that we don't try to re-invent the wheel too many times and that information will be forthcoming by hopefully the end of proceedings today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that is in addition to any information conveyed by Mr. Dixon as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is understood this happen and the informal exchange of information, practical information, is now on the record as it should be. Ms. Issa, are you ready to continue the examination-in-chief of Mr. Bajcetic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whilst that's being done, before Mr. Re leaves the courtroom, I wonder if we might pencil in a point in time during the afternoon session to return to the question of the schedule for next week once the Prosecution have had an opportunity to consider its position.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's what I'm just about to go and do. Of course I'm available at any time this afternoon. I'm making the necessary inquiries now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then we'll hear from you as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bajcetic. I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Ms. Issa will now continue the examination-in-chief. Ms. Issa, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bajcetic.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Bajcetic, we left off when you said at page 108 of the transcript, lines 22 to 25 for the Chamber's reference, that you referred to 30 or even 43 persons were mentioned; therefore, we have to establish where these people were, who had kidnapped them, and whether they were alive at all. And His Honour Judge Orie asked you a question as to how you arrived at that number, 43 persons. I'd like to just deal with that for a few minutes. Without necessarily linking it to the KLA, can you explain when there was a kidnapping in the Dukagjini Zone area in 1998 when you were there, was the RDB Djakovica contacted?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How was the RDB Djakovica contacted?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't want to be continually interrupting Ms. Issa, but this is a question which proceeds from an assumption that a kidnapping has occurred asked for generalisations, not a particular kidnapping or a particular incident but incidents in general, and then asks for a question which is incapable of a sensible answer in terms of how in general terms was the RDB contacted. Because if -- what the witness is being asked to comment on is a pattern of incidents in which missing persons details have been recorded. That is not something that is acceptable of an answer in a form of a generalisation of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, your objection, after having consulted my fellow Judges, is denied. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you answer that question please, sir, how was the RDB contacted if there was a kidnapping in that area?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply speaking, on the basis of the information received from various sources, as I've already explained, from the relatives, from the Albanians who were able to gain such information, or from SUP, all those pieces of information arrived in SUP and then they contacted us because they wanted us to provide assistance, both in the technical and operative sense. We had certain technology, equipment, that made it possible for us where these people were, who had kidnapped them, and whether they were alive at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how many relatives of Albanians would you say approached the RDB in regards to missing persons or kidnappings?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number, but when it comes to those two young people who were found in the canal of Lake Radonjic, I can tell you that they not only did it through their connections and relatives, but they also turned to SUP to provide them assistance in their work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just to clarify that, what are you -- who are you referring to when you say "two young people"?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two young people who were found dead in a car, which was located under the cascade of the canal leading to Lake Radonjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what specific information did you receive in regards to those two young people?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The specific information we received was that the two were a couple, a married couple, Albanians of Catholic faith, who had simply gone missing. So we started searching for them, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when did you receive this information?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this could have been in early September. It's hard for me now to be more specific about the date, but early September of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just to be absolutely clear, when did you receive the information that they were missing?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could have been in late August, not prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And from whom did you receive the information?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received it from the SUP. The RDB received it from SUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were reports regarding -- you mentioned the SUP earlier as well. Were reports regarding missing persons or kidnappings provided to the RDB by the SUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They informed us regularly about that in the hope that we would provide assistance to them in their investigation in the criminal segment of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You also mentioned that you had technology that would assist you in investigating missing persons or kidnappings in this area at that time. Can you be more specific as to what you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the time we had at our disposal certain capabilities for wire-tapping, telephone conversations of those persons whom we believed could provide further details about the whereabouts of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And specifically, can you tell us what time-period you were -- you're referring to when you refer to 43 kidnappings.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the time-period when I was there, that is to say from the 1st of July, 1998, to the 1st of October or 1st of November, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how did you arrive at that figure of 43 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, you are -- in your questions, you're now speaking about kidnappings again, whereas the witness earlier said that they received reports of missing persons or kidnappings. Now, the 43 I understood are under the total category of persons that went missing, and where there may have been suspicions in respect of some or that they might have been kidnapped by whomever, could you please clarify with the witness whether the 43 are the category -- this mixed category, that is all missing and some of them suspicions that they might have been -- or even perhaps even indications that they might have been kidnapped. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, you heard His Honour's question. Are you able to answer that, please?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understood it. We continuously received information about how many people went missing or were kidnapped. It's not like we received all of the information on one day or at one moment. We compiled lists. Sometimes the pieces of information we received were incorrect, and we needed to compare them and reconcile in order to arrive at the most accurate number of people missing and their identities. So we couldn't speak of receiving all of the information at the same time on the same day, no; we received it over a period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, the 43 you were talking about were people that at least went missing and who you identified who they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Based on this information that you refer to, were you able to identify some of those as potential or suspected kidnappings as opposed to people who went missing?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were able. Those were the people who had relatives in Djakovica or who had relatives in SUP, such as the Vlahovic family, Radunovic family, Radosevic family, but we didn't know the exact number of those people who went missing or were kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, I take it that you are aware of what evidence, I would say what better and direct evidence, the Chamber received in view of some of these cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the Chamber doesn't think it is of great assistance to have an indirect report in addition to more direct evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. I'll move on, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, in paragraph 31 of your statement you mention that the Dukagjini area was inaccessible to the MUP police patrols between March 1998 and the end of September 1998 unless an operation was staged. Can you explain why it was inaccessible?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That area was completely inaccessible for the simple reason that it was dominated by the armed formations which had proclaimed themselves as KLA. We used to refer to them as terrorist and rebel groups or sabotage groups. We referred to them in that way because up until the 1st of July they did not have uniforms, nor did they have clear insignia. So we referred to them in this way in order to denote that they were not a military formation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And after the 1st of July?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 1st of July, gradually, not all of them, but gradually they started wearing uniforms and inscription on their sleeves, saying "UCK" or "KLA."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How did you learn this? How do you know that that's --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people who had direct contact with them out on the ground, people who spotted them visually. In addition to that we also received photographs when searching people, or we would simply come across photographs. A lot of them would take photographs of themselves in uniforms and with weapons and we used to come across such photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Are you able to tell us which roads specifically were inaccessible during that period or which roads you were able to access in the Dukagjini area during that period?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Djakovica, Djakovica-Pec road via Decani was not safe because by the village of Rastavica, Babaloc, Crni Breg, Streoc, there were cases of shooting on people travelling in vehicles, be it police or civilians. So everything to the right and to the left of the road from Djakovica to Decani and Pec was not safe, I'm speaking of the village roads. As for the Djakovica-Prizren road, that road was a bit safer because armed people would not appear there -- or at least they would appear in fewer numbers in the vicinity of that road. In addition to this, one couldn't travel towards Pristina on the road going from Pec to Klina and Pristina, nor could one travel from Djakovica through the village of Rakovina towards Pristina. Everybody had to use Djakovica-Prizren-Brezovica and then Prizren road.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: At this point I would like to call-up Exhibit D32, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And perhaps while we're waiting for that, I just want to briefly refer you to paragraph 32 of your statements. In that paragraph, sir, you refer to the 8th September 1998 an operation was mounted by the MUP, you say, in order to investigate the bodies located in the Lake Radonjic area. Then you go on and you say: "Prior to this operation there were regular clashes in this area throughout the time." And I just want you to clarify that. When you say: "Prior to this operation there were regular clashes in this area throughout the time," which area are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring specifically to the area around the village of Istinic, village of Rznic, Glodjane, that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're not referring to the Lake Radonjic area --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's an extraordinarily leading question to put in this context; quite improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes it is. Ms. Issa, would you please withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did that area where regular clashes occurred, sir, include any part of the -- include the Lake Radonjic area?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you be more specific as to what you mean by that. Was the Lake Radonjic area accessible to you during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: To whom?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: To the MUP or to the RDB?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know exactly what triggered it, but there were very fierce clashes sometime in the second half of August of 1998 when certain areas were destroyed. One could see dead animals and so on. Based on that what one could see when going to Lake Radonjic was that there were very serious clashes in that area -- that there had been very serious clashes in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when did those serious clashes begin?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one could say that fierce clashes started on the 1st of July. It's hard to pin-point the date as being the 1st of July, but starting on the 1st of July there erupted fierce clashes between armed Albanians and police forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one clarifying question. In your previous answer you said: "One could see dead animals and so on. Based on that what one could see when going to Lake Radonjic that there had been serious clashes ..." Could you tell us how by going at a certain moment to Lake Radonjic and by seeing dead animals, how you could give a date to these clashes. Or is there other sources of information you used to give us the time-period in which these clashes may have taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot pin-point the date. It's been nine years. However, as we turned off the road to Djakovica-Decani to the right on to an asphalt road, on both sides of that road there were wrecked houses and carcasses. One could observe that clearly. The rubble and carcasses had not been removed by then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you said: "As we turned off the road to Djakovica-Decani to the right," what date are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm speaking of the date when I was there for the first time, which was on the 10th of September, 1998, that was the first time I was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Exhibit D32 is now on your screen, and with perhaps the assistance of Madam Usher, I'd like to ask you if you can circle the area that was inaccessible that you mentioned earlier without mounting or staging an operation.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we blow it up a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we first find the right -- the right picture where the witness thinks he could draw the lines, because once we start marking we can't zoom-in or zoom-out anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore perhaps if we zoom -- is the area, as you said, it was inaccessible without mounting an operation, is that totally visible now on the map you see on the screen or is it a larger area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see the writings here at all. I can see Djakovica, but I really can't make out the place names in the surrounding quadrants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just have a look. Yes. Perhaps we first zoom-in. Would you please tell us when we have zoomed-in to such an extent that still the whole area you would like to mark as the area where you would have no access, when that's on the screen. So could we zoom-in, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There it is. Now I have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the whole of the area you would like to mark is now on the screen? Do I understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you now also read --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the names of the villages and -- are you able to orient yourself on this map now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then -- Ms. Issa, would you give clear instructions to the witness what to mark exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, after you feel comfortable that you've oriented yourself before you begin writing, I would like you to draw a circle around the entire area that was inaccessible without launching or mounting an operation during the period of time that you were there in -- when you were working out of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire area?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is that the entire area or should we actually move the map a little bit further up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that's impossible, as I said before --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we can't -- but we can move it up -- we can certainly not zoom-in and out. And whether we can move it, I'm not quite certain. No, we can't move it either.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you confirm, Mr. Bajcetic, whether that's the entire area that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is most of the area. We can see Decani, Djakovica, and the villages to the right and to the left of the road. Junik was quite inaccessible. It's a pretty large village, then beyond that one, we can see it here, was the villages of Dobros. And then the other villages, Dujak, Zdrelo, Glamoc, Dubrava, Glodjane, Rznic, Pozar, Gornji and Donji Ratis, Dasinovac, Zabelj, Jablanica, these are all the villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I would like to tender that as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be P379, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against admission? No. Then it is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, I'd like to now move to paragraph 36 of your statement. In paragraph 35 you mention that two KLA fighters that had been arrested, Ljulj Musaj and Zenelj Alija provided information about the Lake Radonjic and Dasinovac site and then in paragraph 36 you say that this information from the two KLA members confirmed previous information about missing or kidnapped persons. Can you explain exactly what this previous information was.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When such large numbers of people go missing, of course it becomes the focus of attention and then the information is collected in various ways. First of all, there's the family. I mentioned Rade Vlahovic as one of the individuals whose families were killed, and then I mentioned Momcilo Stijovic who was a police officer and had his family in the area. He was in touch with Albanians who were able to provide him with information. He was on friendly terms with some of them. I was able to see that for myself. Then we had information collected through our technology and then through our operative work in the field, through our associates, and it was on the basis of these pieces of information that we decided in which direction to turn our investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But apart from referring to information or intelligence as to missing persons, did you have any other information that caused you to confirm -- that was confirmed by the information that was provided by Alija and Musaj?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part information I referred to so far, it was Ljulj Musaj and Zenelj Alija who provided crucial information. We decided to follow-up on that and to verify the veracity of the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. You mentioned that Rade Vlahovic and Momcilo Stijovic provided information regarding missing family members. Who exactly are Rade Vlahovic and Momcilo Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Vlahovic was a policeman who worked for the civilian department. His parents went missing at the time. Momcilo Stijovic was also a policeman from the area who was a uniformed police officer. My impression was that both of them had been on friendly terms from some Albanians from the area before the conflict and during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What do you base that impression on?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To put it simply, I base it on the fact that at the time I heard from Momcilo Stijovic himself that the Albanians had helped him to transport some of his belongings out of his house by tractor. This was part of his effort to evacuate his belongings from the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Apart from Zenelj Alija and Ljulj Musaj, were you aware of any other KLA members that had been arrested by the MUP who provided similar information?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of that. I just don't know the identity of the man. It was on the 8th that the MUP had taken him to Lake Radonjic, it wasn't us, that's why I don't know his identity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And why were Alija and Musaj turned over to the RDB?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the MUP did not cover that professional part of arriving at information in an analytical way. We were far more professional and experienced in that area of work and it was our job to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm going to paragraph 20 of your statement, Mr. Bajcetic. You say that you received information about the command structure of the KLA through documents that were seized by the RDB in the manner that you describe in paragraph 18 of your statement and from members of the KLA who had been arrested. Can you explain what that information was that you received?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wherever the armed Albanians retreated, they left documents behind. At that point in time, we had in our possession large amounts of documents. The documents predominantly related to the formation of groups engaged in illegal trafficking of weapons from Albania into Kosovo. We knew when they were supposed to go and where. We knew which people were engaged in digging up trenches. There were orders addressing certain persons and telling them where to go and who to report to. Simply, these were documents that we were able to find in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, we don't have these documents, do we?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't whether these are documents the same as some of the documents we have seen, do we?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't believe so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Now, this witness is interpreting documents. Now we have heard quite a bit of direct and better evidence, where we have seen quite some documents. To what extent would it assist the Chamber to hear the interpretation of unknown documents, perhaps the same, perhaps different ones, by a witness where we have had quite a lot of witnesses who testified about structures. So to that extent it -- I wonder whether it's of great use to pursue the matter in the way we're doing at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. Of course if there's any concrete matter, if you say I saw a document, this document, dated that and that day giving orders there, then we have the problem that we don't have the document. But that's of course from saying I've seen a lot of documents about where to go, what to do, that's -- it's rather vague. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, in your statements, you say that you visited the crime sites of Lake Radonjic canal, the Ekonomija farm, and Dasinovac. You also say that you viewed video-clips of these sites before at some point and also you viewed video-clips of these sites in Belgrade when you gave a related statement in May of 2007. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to call-up Exhibit P72, please. It's actually a video. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is from Dasinovci and this is Zenelj Alija.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You can just stop there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So is this the same video, sir, you viewed previously, which is referred to in the statement, which includes the --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- the 10th and the 8th and the 9th as well?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one from Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Issa. I may have missed something, but the dates and the times on this video are rather confusing. I do understand that it has been reconstructed because some of these pictures certainly are not taken at 3.00 in the morning. Is there any agreement on this reconstruction, or is there not, and has it yet been fully explained to the Chamber, because we're looking again and again at pictures.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can clarify that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's actually -- the explanation is contained in Mr. Bajcetic's 92 ter statement, and it's quite --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you point me to the paragraph then?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Might the witness remove his earphones for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please take off your earphones for a second, Mr. Bajcetic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, it starts at paragraph 79.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then 80; and if you look at paragraph 83 in particular, it -- there's an explanation as to how much time is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say it's a.m. and p.m., which has been --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, there is a 12-hour difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That doesn't explain the difference in dates, does it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, it does, because of the 12-hour difference, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 12 hours earlier or later?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Twelve hours later, as explained in paragraph 82.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I can certainly explore this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Twelve hours later of the actual time. That's at least what this witness told us. Mr. Emmerson, is there any --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is there any agreement on it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The answer to that is no aspect of the evidence in relation to this part of the case is agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And there's another witness who is about to give evidence who gives a different explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Clearly, the time shown on the counter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could not be --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- could not be the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's the only, I think, you could agree upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we know where we stand. Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to cross-examine Mr. Bajcetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Oh, I'm sorry. Please put on your earphones again. You'll now be

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I just wondered if it would be possible to, perhaps, provide the witness with a copy of the Serbian version of his statement, in the event he will be cross-examined on his statement to be completely fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is behind tab 14 in the yellow file.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We actually have a copy which we could provide to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, there are more documents to be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And this one is in the yellow binder which will be provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is another binder to be provided, volume 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Volume 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- which is a brown binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, binders are provided to you. You're supposed to look at those portions when Mr. Emmerson invites you to do so; and if he doesn't invite you, just leave them as they are. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For -- by way of explanation, the yellow binder you have in front of you is volume 1, and you're about to be handed a brown binder which is volume 2. So when I refer to volume 2, I'm referring to the brown binder. Could we start, please, by looking at your witness statement in these proceedings, which is behind tab 14 in the yellow binder and which you signed on the 24th of May of this year. And, perhaps, you would turn to paragraph 18, first of all. Do you have that? Mr. Bajcetic, do you have paragraph 18?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to go through that with you, please, if I may, for a moment. You say in paragraph 18: "The public police (MUP) in cooperation with our operatives seized documents from the KLA of precise information on who smuggled weapons." You say: "I cannot remember exactly which house they entered first because they entered several houses and seized documentation. This was done regularly throughout the period of time I was there, starting from July 1998." Pause there. Now, first of all, just so that we're clear, you've told us that you were there from the 1st of July until either the 1st of October or the 1st of November. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And what's the reason for the uncertainty as to whether it's the 1st of October or the 1st of November?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the simple reason that nine years have elapsed since. I didn't consult the document posting me down there or the one which records the date when I returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. But during the time you were there, these seizures would happen -- of documents would happen regularly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How regularly? Can you give us a sense? Twice? Three times a week? More or less than that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One cannot put it that way, whether it was twice or three times a week; rather, it was at the time when an operation was being carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that. I just want to have a sense of how often those seizures would occur. Use whatever formulation is most convenient to you.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's put it at once or twice a week, but these were continuous activities in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that. And they were activities conducted jointly by the MUP acting in conjunction with your operatives, is that correct? That's what you say in your statement "our operatives took part."

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And by your "operatives," let's be clear, are you speaking about employees of the RDB from Djakovica or are you speaking about armed forces of the JSO?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking solely of the RDB members from Djakovica who were seconded by several operatives from Belgrade, or rather, who were assisted by several operatives from Belgrade. And they always went into the field in civilian clothes with SUP members.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With armed officers?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police was armed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And just while we're on that subject, you know that the JSO was part of the RDB at this point, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that area in the period we're discussing, there was never any JSO. We're talking about the period between the 1st of July and the 1st of October or the 1st of November. In that period of time, the JSO was never stationed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, that's a lie, isn't it? There was a JSO barracks just outside Decan, which was observed --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I'm sorry. Not in Djakovica, but in Decan?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain about Decani either. I can tell you one piece of information that I know for a fact: That in Dubrava prison, that's where it was stationed, I'm not certain about Decani, but I know about Djakovica that there weren't any for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we've heard evidence in this courtroom that the JSO had a barracks just outside Decan. Are you saying that that's not true or you didn't know one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that I didn't know either way. I certainly didn't visit the barracks to know. I'm not -- I know about Djakovica, that there weren't any, and I heard about Dubrava near Istok and I know that there were some there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The JSO was part of the RDB at this time, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you never see an officer of the JSO at any time whilst you were in Kosovo between the 1st of July and the time that you left in October or November?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't in touch with them, was I?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So coming back to paragraph 18, these operations that were being conducted once or twice a week, if we look at the bottom of that paragraph and it lists the areas where they were being conducted: "Smonica, Jablanica, Rastavica, Babaloc, Dujak, Skivjan, Reka Kec, Glodjane, and Rznic." So can we take it, therefore, then that those areas were being entered by the forces you have described once or twice a week during the period between the 1st of July and the time when you left Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this period, the period on discussion here, they didn't enter all these villages all at the same time, at any point in time. It really depended on where the police had been attacked or maybe there had been an attack to the civilians; and in such cases, one went to those villages. Like this, there was no reason to cause another conflict, and that's why one didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, but the forces of the Serbian police could go there and did go there when the need arose. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever the need arose, that's right. If there was an attack, for example, if civilians had come under threat, in those cases they did go, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as you've told Ms. Issa in your evidence just a little while ago, that included from the 1st of July a number of clashes between Albanian forces and Serbian forces. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you gave us a description of the areas where those clashes occurred during this period from the 1st of July, and that included the area around Gllogjan and Irzniq and Lake Radoniq?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we just look at paragraph 29 of your witness statement, you explain that in a little more detail, I think. You say: "From March 1998 onwards, the fighting between the MUP and the KLA continued, and it particularly intensified from the 1st of July." You say that many roads were unsafe, that the KLA carried out attacks on the police, and on civilians you say. You say: "This happened almost on a daily basis, mostly on the roads and junction and crossroads. Sometimes," you say," the MUP returned fire and other times the MUP would organise the operation the next day and some persons were arrested." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting to that because it's unclear whether paragraph 29 actually refers to any of the areas that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just about to ask --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- my colleague just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that Mr. Emmerson intends to clarify that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, presumably the people who were arrested were believed to be members of the KLA. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believed to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but not all were always necessarily members, were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But they were believed to be either members of the KLA or supporters of the KLA who had engaged in armed attacks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And these would be people who were located within the areas either side of the main road that you've described as being areas which the KLA mainly controlled. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so the operations that were taking place on the 1st of July involved, if I can put it, arrest operations going into those areas. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that would include, would it, the areas you've described of Gllogjan, Irzniq, and the Lake Radoniq canal on the eastern side of the main road?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the right-hand side of the Djakovica-Decani road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It would include operations into those areas. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've given the 1st of July as a date from which this process began to intensify. Can you just explain to us, was it from the 1st of July, to your knowledge, that the number of clashes increased?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 1st of July that I arrived in Djakovica --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it was roughly that around that time the clashes intensified.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And that was information presumably that you acquired in your capacity as deputy head of the RDB Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was assistant chief of the RDB in Djakovica. On account of the growing intensity of the clashes, the central office in Belgrade decided to reinforce the Djakovica set-up in purely operational terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But my question, Mr. Bajcetic, is: In your capacity as assistant chief, you were kept informed of these operations taking place and the clashes that were taking place. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was common knowledge. We were all in the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew what the areas were in which clashes were occurring. There was no surprise factor in it, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And then we turn, if we may, to paragraph 32 when you say this: "On the 8th of September, 1998, an operation was mounted by the MUP in order to investigate the bodies located in the Lake Radonjic area. Prior to this operation, there were regular clashes in this area throughout the time. This area was not accessible until an operation was mounted." Is that the same period of time that you're describing these clashes taking place; in other words, from the 1st of July?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And sometimes they would involve arrests. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And sometimes they would involve the seizure of documents?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And sometimes they would involve fire-fights between the KLA and the Serbian forces in those areas?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's how it was for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And quite fierce fire-fights from time to time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were the PJP involved in those types of operations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Mr. Emmerson's just asked a series of rather vague questions because he's -- he hasn't specified a specific time-period or what specific areas he's referring to, and it -- it's a little unclear at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we look at the context of it, you earlier made an observation there, Ms. Issa. I did noted at that time respond when you said 29 makes it unclear what area we're talking about. If you look for paragraph 30 where, for example, Babaloc and Rastavica are specifically mentioned, and we know where that's situated. If you look at 31: "From a security point of view, the Dukagjini area had therefore become." So if we read it in the context, I think there's no great confusion about it. And I think Mr. Emmerson as far as time is concerned asked whether that was on from the 1st of July, as the witness testified when the -- when the clashes intensified. So I think that is what Mr. Emmerson is asking the witness about. If he understands that differently, if there's any confusion, I'd like to know. And, Mr. Emmerson, if I misunderstood your questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour is quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I would like to know as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I had asked the witness about a number of specific locations, including Gllogjan and Irzniq and the Lake Radoniq canal, and I think the witness has answered them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must add to that that often we talk about the Dukagjini area or Dukagjini Zone. Sometimes it's a reference to administrative matters rather than anything else. The Lake Radonjic area is not always sufficiently defined.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I used the expression "Lake Radoniq canal area."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, not always today a reference was made to the Lake Radonjic canal area; and even if you're talking about the canal area, where does it stop? Does it stop after two kilometres? Does it stop after ten kilometres? So, therefore, for the future not to revisit any questions, if reference is made to the Lake Radonjic area or the Lake Radonjic canal area, I would like to know what are the limits of that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, did the forces conducting these operations include the PJP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This is a matter for the SUP. I'm not sure if they got them involved or not. I wasn't a party at those meetings. I had nothing to do with the SUP operations. We had a different kind of cooperation. Whenever they arrested someone, they submit an assessment to us and that's how our cooperation went in general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, we've heard evidence in this case that there were Serb forces, both VJ and MUP, stationed in the area of Lake Radoniq canal. Did you see those forces yourself or not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt again, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But I think the for the purpose of that question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- he needs to indicate when he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I would like there, perhaps, a bit more precision, Mr. Emmerson, both in terms of where the Lake Radonjic canal area is. Could you, please, refer to the evidence or the places where these forces were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Absolutely. I was going to ask him if he had seen them so he could assist with those questions. But if Your Honour would like me to put specifics to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would very much like to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, were you aware or did you personally see VJ or MUP forces stationed on Radonicka Suka, sometimes called Suka Bitesh, an area of elevated ground on the western side of Lake Radoniq?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only time I saw any military men was on the 10th --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- If September 1998 when they were securing the area, when they secured the area. They were deployed in a ring, and then down the depth of the area. Therefore, they weren't necessarily readily apparent as a military district formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. That's what you saw. Now, in your capacity as assistant chief of the RDB Gjakove, were you aware of the fact that there were VJ and MUP forces stationed on a hill immediately to the west of Lake Radoniq?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is in Babaloc there was a police station. I know that for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there once on my way to Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So my question is: The operations that you've described taking place between the 1st of July and the time when you left on a regular basis, where would they launch from?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you about what I saw for myself. Some of those operations were launched from --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name of the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name you just mentioned. Launched from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, first, since I'd like to discuss some timing issues, but we don't need you for that. So could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. And we'll have a break for approximately 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could you give us an indication on how much time you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think I've been cross-examining for about 15 minutes or thereabouts, perhaps a little bit longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A little bit longer I think, but we can check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have enough cross-examination for this witness to last the rest of the afternoon, but I'm -- and taking account of the fact that I know Mr. Guy-Smith has some questions for him there will be some re-examination. My aim would be to adjust the timing so we can complete the witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber considered whether it would be possible to finish the witness for today. The Chamber is a bit concerned that there might be a lot of pushing at the very end, also for re-examination. The subject of the testimony seems to be of great importance to this case. There's another matter that the Chamber has considered not to sit after the second break --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- for reasons unrelated to this case. The Chamber would have continued after the second break under Rule 15 bis if the Chamber would have been confident if we could conclude the witness without pushing and rushing too much today. The Chamber is not confident that that is possible. Under those circumstances, where 15 bis should not be applied -- yes, if it would not help us out to make the witness return before the weekend, we would -- I do understand that my fellow Judges would not consider it to be in the interest of justice to continue. That's not within my competence to decide that, but that's whispered in my ear from the right-hand side, that there would be no unanimity on the interests of justice being served by continuing. Therefore, under those circumstances, the Chamber will not try to finish this witness today where we often make a great effort to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I may say so, I'm extremely grateful for that, because he is a witness who needs careful examination and not to be placed under the sort of time pressure that sometimes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And also because re-examination might suffer from it. So it's fine that you're grateful, but that, of course, would be the totality of the testimony. Apart from that the Chamber does not know yet whether we will have any questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So under those circumstances, we are not going to rush to get him returned to his own place before the weekend. This is not an invitation or an encouragement to take one minute more than needed. We'll have a break until quarter past 4.00, but, Mr. Kearney, if there would be already some information from Mr. Re on next week, the position of the Prosecution on the next week witnesses, then the Chamber would like to hear it now so that we can consider it over the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I was just rising to discuss that issue, Your Honour. I'm going to meet with Mr. Re right now. I'll have hopefully some guidance for the Trial Chamber when we resume. But just to be clear, today we are not going to here, be sitting in the third session that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what the Trial Chamber -- we'll finish then at approximately quarter past 5.00, 20 minutes past 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is the Trial Chamber's thought to bring this witness back on Monday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if we're not finished by then, and it's very unlikely that we would be finished by then, the witness to return on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And of course we -- I don't know whether you have any indication whether the witness would have to travel back before the weekend. Is there any indication that he could not remain until Monday?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's no indication one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's then clear. Mr. Kearney, if your position -- if you have discussed the position with Mr. Re three or four lines in an e-mail would inform the Chamber already in such a way that we do not lose time unnecessarily after the break, and we'll give an opportunity to the Defence as well to consider its position. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll have a break until quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [The witness takes the stand].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, there are a few matters which are not relevant for you which I'd like to deal with very quickly. We have received the motion to exclude ballistics. We first have to read it, so there's no way to discuss it at this moment. Then we have seen that there's a notification of an expert report under Rule 94 bis which is related to the other issue. Then finally, we have received Prosecution's motion for testimony in relation to Witness 55, that's testimony through videolink. Yesterday I think Defence expressed that they did not as such object testimony through videolink, but of course that I would give an opportunity to comment on reasons. Having read it, I would be surprised if we would have a lengthy debate on the reasons given. I see that -- well, if there's any need to further discuss the reasons, then the Chamber will hear from you, but we will proceed with the matter. Then, Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, could you turn again to your own witness statement to paragraph 38, please. Paragraph 38 you describe how two individuals, Alija and Musaj, I think that's Zenelj Alija and Ljulj Musaj were arrested by the MUP in the beginning of September, and you say that you're not personally aware of the circumstances under which they were arrested. That's an accurate statement of the position, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please look at paragraph 39. You say: "After they were arrested, the MUP handed over both KLA members to the RDB Djakovica because of their KLA membership and their involvement in terrorist activities. This happened at the very beginning of September 1998." Now, pausing there, what happened at the very beginning of September?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened was they were arrested in the early days of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And your statement continues: "Bogdan Tomas from the RDB Djakovica interrogated them. I did not carry out the interrogation, but I briefly attended the interrogations from time to time for a few days before the 8th of September, 1998." Now, pause there for a moment. I think you say a little later on that these men were interrogated by the MUP before they were handed over to the RDB. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you personally ever attend any of the MUP interviews?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So going back to that sentence there, where you say you briefly attended the interrogations from time to time for a few days before the 8th of September, obviously, we know that the testimony or the account is these men were taken to the canal on the 8th of September. Can you give us a sense of how many days? When you say a few days before that, how many days before that you entered into interrogations.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
