utterances.text: I can't say specifically how many days before. It was a long time ago; but if you bear in mind the legal framework, what the law provides for in terms of how long they could be kept, I guess it would be several days.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Plainly, it's more than one day. Can you help us as to whether it was two or three?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be more specific. I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- It just wouldn't be right for me to improvise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand. But you are clear, because you talk about there being more than one interrogation over a few days, you are clear that they were -- you entered into interrogations over more than one day?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My role was like this: Whenever I was called by one of the operative officers, Bogdan Tomas and the late Dejan Jovovic in this case, I would come in to study the certain types of information or perhaps to retrieve information that I would then cross-reference that to other information I may have had.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand what your role was. You entered into the interrogations from time to time; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My question is: In your statement, you say that took place in relation to interrogations, in the plural, that went on for a few days. And I'm asking you, please, to confirm that those interrogations went on for more than one day.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than one day, yes, with breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And you are referring to more than one day before the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you're referring also to interrogations conducted by Mr. Tomas?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas and the late Dejan Jovovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at paragraph 40, you say: "After they were arrested the prosecutor and investigating judge prescribed a three-day detention for them according to the law. During the three days, they were interrogated by the RDB; but, initially, they had been interrogated by the MUP." You see that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in relation to that part of your statement, were you aware, at the time that they were handed over to the RDB, that they had already been interviewed by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of that. At the time, they surrendered them to us because we were told explicitly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if you look very briefly, just to cast an eye, behind tab 5 in that bundle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. Witness, you said: "I was aware of that. At the time they surrendered them to us because, we were told explicitly." Who is "we"? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We, the people from the State Security Sector, and I also mean the people from SUP who were the ones handing these people over to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the people from the State Security Sector who were told about the prior interviews, would that include yourself and Mr. Tomas?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I'm saying is I had no part in that. It wasn't my job to conduct interviews. My job was to analyse. My job was to provide assistance to those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we're talking about at cross-purposes. Let me take you back a moment ago. You said a moment ago that when these men were handed over to the RDB, you were told explicitly that they had already been interviewed, and you said "we were told" that they had already been interviewed. And Judge Hoepfel asked you: Who do you mean by "we"? And you replied: "e, the people from the State Security Sector." Yes?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So when they were handed over to you, that is to say, the people from the State Security Sector, by the MUP, the MUP officers who handed them over told you that they had already been interviewed. That's the position, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did they -- when you say "we" in that context, was that something that Mr. Tomas was told, as well as yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was stated -- rather, Mr. Camovic was the head of that particular department. No person could be surrendered to any else of a lower rank. He was the one to be informed and he received whoever was being handed over, and then he decided who would be dealing with that person from then -- from there on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you involved in process of selecting Mr. Tomas as the person who would do the interviews?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In most cases, Mr. Camovic did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Camovic told you that these men had already been interviewed by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, this was nine years ago. I suppose he told me that. I can't remember that detail, but he must have told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's clear that you knew that because you said so in your statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look behind tab 5, there is just -- I don't ask you to look at the contents of it, but there is a statement made by one of these men or signed by one of these men --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- which is dated the 4th of September, but refers to an interview on the 3rd. And, I think, if you look at the end, you may recognise the names as members of the MUP, is that correct, Zivojin Stankovic and Dusan Dragovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So presumably is it right to assume that when the men are handed over to the RDB, the statement would be handed over with them so that you have an idea of what they've already said?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presumably. I don't remember the detail, but I presume that that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, it would be a very strange thing indeed, wouldn't it, if the MUP had already interviewed these men in Djakovica police station to hand them over to you without giving you copies of the statements that they had signed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa. Before you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm objecting to that, Your Honour. I think he's asking the witness to speculate. The witness already indicated he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Let me just re-read the question. The question doesn't call for speculation. The question is, as a matter of fact, what would the usual thing be, and then of course if it went otherwise then that would be strange because not be the usual thing. It doesn't say anything about what happened so to that extent there's no call for speculation. You may answer the question whether it would be strange if he would have been interviewed already or that they would have been -- these men would have been interviewed already without the statements being given to you. That would be not the ordinary thing you would expect. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be strange not to give statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if we look at paragraph 72 of your witness statement, can I understand from you the position, Mr. Bajcetic, whilst Mr. Tomas was conducting these interviews, was he sending at the end of each day some sort of dispatch?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he came by important information, then he did; otherwise, he would verbally report on the results of these interviews at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: By "verbally," you mean orally? It was translated into English as "verbally."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This means that we would sit down at the end of the day, and he would inform us of the information he came by during these interviews.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, Mr. Emmerson. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, we've seen certain documents that were compiled and have dates upon them, and I won't go with you into the complications or the difficulties with the dates. But any document that was compiled contemporaneously, that is to say on the day that an interview took place, any such document would be a dispatch. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which document you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm simply you if Mr. Tomas recorded anything in writing on the day, that would be in the form of a dispatch. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He could have made notes during such interviews and then assessed that none of these matters called for an urgent analysis. However, if he came by information that was significant for the investigation, he would send it off in a concise form.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And send it off in a dispatch. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a telegram, which would later be substantiated by a written document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you say in paragraph 72 that all of the dispatches that were made at that time were destroyed after a retention period of one year. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that something you know about these dispatches specifically? Have you been able to conduct a search in relation to them, or are you merely just describing general practice?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a general practice, too, but on the other hand we did -- we were not legally required to retain these telegrams because the contents of the telegrams were reflected in an official note or in any other sort of document which was then permanently kept in the records.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so these dispatches were sent from Djakovica to Prizren and then from Prizren to Pristina and Belgrade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So there would be four separate sites holding these dispatches at any one time. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite correct. The same contents thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And all four of these sites would have destroyed the dispatches. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, that's the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you know in fact whether that is the position in respect of these dispatches? Or let me put it another way. Do you know in fact whether that is the position in respect of dispatches that were filed during September 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that explicitly because I was neither charged with keeping telegrams in the records or destroying them. This was the standard working practice. Whatever was contained in a telegram had to be reflected in a document which was permanently kept. The telegram as such carried no value.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we look, please, at paragraph 36 and 37 of your witness statements together. Now, remind yourself of what is written there just for a moment and see if, having done that, you can help me with one or two matters. You say in paragraph 36 that the information that is recorded to have been provided by these two men was linked - if I can put it that way - but the RDB to information that had previously been provided by two police officers, Momcilo Stijovic and Rade Vlahovic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think the view that was taken was that effectively these two were confirming information you'd already received from those two men. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was quite clear on this matter. Information was being gathered continuously from relatives, from individual Albanians, from intelligence-gathering technology, and all the information was cross-referenced in order to establish whether a certain event did transpire or not and in what way it transpired. And that's the only way one can put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So I understand that, but in paragraphs 36, 37, and at the bottom of paragraph 39 of your witness statement you isolate and identify those two police officers as the source of information that you already had. Is that a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And both of those police officers, to your knowledge, believed their own relatives to have been killed by the KLA and dumped in the Lake Radoniq canal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. It's true that that's what they believed. First of all, Rade Vlahovic whose parents were kidnapped by the KLA, or so he believed, and he was concerned about their fate. At that point in time, he did not know where they had been dumped, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware that Rade Vlahovic had been assigned to conduct the interviews of some of these men?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just look behind tab 15 for a moment. Don't mention the name of the person who made this statement, but just look at the name at the front. You see the author of the statement; yes? Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Read it for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you see that? Do you know who that individual is?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You don't. Very well. Well, without going into the details at this point in open session, that is a -- that individual was a crime technician working for the SUP in Gjakove in connection with this inquiry and with the arrests of these men. All right. You can assume that that's the position. If you can turn to paragraph 30: "The interviews of these terrorists were led by crime inspectors of SUP Djakovica. I recall Radovan Zlatkovic" -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you have paragraph number 30 behind tab 15? Are you behind tab 15? Maybe the usher might help you. Tab 15, paragraph 30 in the statement. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. So it reads: "The interviews of these terrorists were led by the crime inspectors of SUP Djakovica. I recall Radovan Zlatkovic, Dusan Dragovic, Rade Vlahovic, and Ljubisa Novovic being involved in these interviews. I also remember that interviews were also conducted by the state security police officers, but I don't remember their names." Now, we've seen that Dusan Dragovic signed one of the witness statements because we looked at that a moment ago, and you can see here that Rade Vlahovic was involved in the interviews.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry to rise again, but I think Mr. Emmerson needs to be specific which interview Rade Vlahovic was involved in. He's referring to interviews in general without being specific as to who he is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a first question that is permissible and if there do not follow any further details there might remain a question mark but as such the question is admissible.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There will be other evidence in relation to that. This witness may or may not know the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understood you to have said, Mr. Bajcetic, that you didn't know that Rade Vlahovic was assigned to this interview process at all. Is that correct? It wasn't something you knew at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you have regarded it as appropriate for a police officer who was so personally involved in an investigation to the extent that he believed his own parents to have been killed and put in the canal to have been assigned to the process of interviewing the suspects?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think that's a slight misrepresentation. The witness had earlier said that Rade Vlahovic didn't know where his relatives were dumped.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I can find the line of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness added that's what he believed -- no, he did not know at that time, that's what the said. At that time he did not know whether -- he believed that they were abducted by the KLA, and he did not know where they were dumped. I think that's -- but I could check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Maybe I can clarify with the witness. The answer I think that Your Honour has in mind is page 55, line 15 --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It begins with: "It's true, that's what they believed" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps I can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it right that the information that you had been provided with before these men were arrested from Rade Vlahovic, was first of all that he believed his parents had been abducted by the KLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He believed that, but he did not have precise information because he could not reach the home of his parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did he have any belief as to what had been done with their bodies?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I did not discuss this with him in such detail that he might tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the objection by Ms. Issa I think referred to page 55, lines 15 up to and including line 18, where specific --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a specific answer is given as far as knowledge of the place where they were dumped.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: To put the question to you again. In the context of an investigation of this kind, would it have been considered -- would you have considered it appropriate for a police officer to conduct interviews in those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why this question is put to me. I did not and could not take part in the discussions within the SUP as to who they would bring in or who they would interview.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your last sentence because the interpreters could not hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was whether I would in principle accept a person who has a personal interest in a case to take part in it. I said that I could not play any role in the selection of persons to take part in interviews within MUP, and I did not discuss these matters with them, because I wasn't interested and this wasn't part of my job. That's why I can't give a specific answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the question is at the edge --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of opinion and facts --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please move on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You speak here about the existence of prior intelligence, and I want to ask you if you could help us to understand one or two documents that relate to that for a moment. First of all, David Gajic was the head of the RDB in Kosovo, was he not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a coordinator.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that different from being the head of the RDB in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you what his exact role was. Officially he was a coordinator.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In practical terms was there anybody more senior to him within the RDB in Kosovo itself?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn please briefly behind tab 12 for a moment. And, in fact, may I just clarify this because Ms. Issa gave some information earlier on. Is it correct that you don't speak or read any English?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the typed English version -- and this is pages 86 and 87 of 164 - bear with me for a moment - those are minutes that you have in front of you in Serbian for the Joint Command bringing together the RDB, the VJ, the MUP, and senior politicians. And if you can find the entry for the 4th of September, please.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page is that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you like just to pass the bundle over to me for one moment, and I'll find it for you. I'm afraid ...

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which page that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you just bring it to me for one moment, I'll find the relevant page and open it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, there is an entry there in manuscript at the bottom of the left-hand page - in our copy it is the top of the right-hand page - from Mr. Gajic. Do you see that? Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to have it on the record, I take it that you have drawn the attention of the witness to page K0228486.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see the entry at the bottom there, Mr. Bajcetic? Yes?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look to the facing page, the text continues. And at the fifth bullet point, Mr. Gajic reports that in the village of Ratis near Decani there is a mass graveyard, 34 Serbs, three Romanies, three Albanians, that is making 40 individuals in all. Now, can you help us at all as to how Mr. Gajic could have come by that information, given that you were RDB in Gjakove, as early as the 4th of September?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't account for this at all for the simple reason that it happened nine years ago, and it's very difficult to retrace all these different dates. What I just said can be found in the documents. You can see when interviews were held with the two individuals, when we went out into the field. I can't know about Mr. Gajic's contacts or his whereabouts. I was not in touch with him nor was that part of my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But the presumably the information was being provided by RDB Gjakove. Would that not be the normal method of reporting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Mr. Emmerson's now asking the witness to speculate. He's just indicated he simply does not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you can ask him -- whether the witness knows whether the information was provided by --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was going to ask him about the normal system of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If there was information coming from the RDB to Mr. Gajic concerning events in the area of Ratis, that would be information which would come from which part of the RDB, Gjakove or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information could have originated from the RDB in Pec --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because we were one and the same centre, Prizren, in that Pec and we both provided information.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this: Can you now, looking back on those events, conceive of any means by which specific numbers of remains could have been communicated to Mr. Gajic by the RDB as early as the 4th of September?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's a speculative question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me re-read it. If you reformulate the question, you might obtain the information you would like to have, but whether the witness can conceive of any means --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- is speculative. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Based on your own knowledge of what was taking place in RDB Djakovica in the period from the 1st to the 8th of September, is there anything that you know of which could account for Mr. Gajic having been told by RDB subordinates of a specific number of remains?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Mr. Emmerson asked this question in a different form earlier on and the witness indicated he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's then verify whether it was exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, it has not been ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't possibly know that. I wasn't the chief of the centre in Prizren in order to be able to know where the information came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the answer now is that he couldn't know. The question was whether you did know, but I take it that the witness has now clearly said that he --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He doesn't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- doesn't know any such thing. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just this, you've mentioned now twice two different locations, you've mentioned RDB Prizren and RDB Pec as possible sources of information being provided to Mr. Gajic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I must tell you what this is about. There's the Prizren centre, which in terms of territory covered Metohija or the following towns: Prizren, Orahovac, Djakovica, Pec, Istok, and Klina. So that is the centre, the HQ, which had branches in Djakovica and in Pec. I in Djakovica couldn't know what somebody was sending over from Pec or from Prizren for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's understood. And so far as you are aware, did the RDB operatives in Prizren or Pec go to the canal area before your team?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we turn to tab 17 in the yellow file, please. This is a witness statement made by Mr. Gajic commenting on that entry in the minutes. And the paragraphs are numbered according to the days of the minutes, and if you could find paragraph 26, please. Commenting - this is page 15 for those of us following it in English - commenting on that entry in the minutes against his own name Mr. Gajic is recorded as saying this: "The RDB had received information about this mass grave in Ratis, although it was never clear if some of those bodies were thrown later on in the canal near Radonjicko Lake. This information was provided to the RDB by the head of our local office, Vule Mircic. I do not know whether those bodies were ever found in Ratis." Now, first of all, which local office was Vule Mircic the head of?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the head of the Decani SUP department or office.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So when Mr. Gajic refers to him as being "head of our local office," he's actually referring to somebody who's not a member of the RDB. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not Vule Mircic. He was the head of the Pec SUP local office.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any information that might throw any light on this suggestion, that bodies might have been moved from Ratis into the canal?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe that that's what the statement says; it's a misrepresentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, that's sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any information that could throw light on the suggestion that there was a mass grave in Ratis although there was no clarity about whether any of the bodies were thrown later on in the canal near Radoniq Lake?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't be expected to say anything about it. I only know what I saw on the 10th of September, when I was actually there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to move on now back to your own witness statement for a moment, if I may, which is just to remind you is tab 14. Could you turn to paragraphs 42 to 47 for a moment. I just want to see if I can get some clarification from you about these paragraphs. Is it the position that on the 8th of September the detachment of RDB officials that had gone to the canal returned to you that evening and reported what they had seen?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was being very specific when I said ten members of the MUP and the RDB. They left on the 8th of September. Mr. Tomas led these men so they could show it to us. We had not been able to pin-point the exact spot until we were shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You personally didn't go on that reconnaissance trip on the 8th, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the information that you've recorded in your statement about what happened on that day is information that Mr. Tomas and his colleagues provided to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it right that they provided that information to you when they returned to Djakovica police station that evening?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The RDB that evening, it was in the RDB offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And that would be Mr. Tomas, Mr. Jovovic, and the video cameraman who was with them, would it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you help us, was that the first information you received about what had happened and what they had seen that day?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, that was the first information telling us what they had seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the first time you were brought into the loop of information about what had been seen at the canal that day was when they got back and told you, was it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Specific information about what they had seen, the bodies, the location of the bodies, this is precisely what they told me that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that. The question I'm asking you was: Before they got back to the police station, had you been receiving information during the afternoon about what they'd seen or was it only when they got the back that evening that the information was conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no one to tell me that afternoon, although some had already arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just clarify that answer, if you would, for a moment. You were at Djakovica police station during that day; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the RDB offices in Djakovica. Those people were sent out. As soon as they were back, they told us about what they had seen --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that is the accurate version of the story.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And you were not provided with any information, for example, by telephone or by radio during the afternoon, is that the position? You first learnt about it that evening?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BAJCETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. There was no coverage there for mobile phones. Radio links were difficult as well because there were problems with the transmission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I noticed - I'm addressing you, Mr. Kearney - that where the Chamber asked for if only one or two lines as far as the position of -- for next week would be, that at least until two minutes ago I didn't receive anything by e-mail. I don't know how much time you would need. The Chamber would like to adjourn in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just being shown by my colleague an e-mail that was sent at 5.08 p.m. by Mr. Re, so perhaps the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we then already excuse the witness and see what the message is. Mr. Bajcetic, a bit earlier than usual we have to stop for the day, and since the Chamber is not sitting tomorrow we would like to see you back Monday. I earlier asked the office of the -- I'm sorry. Yes. Mr. Bajcetic, a bit earlier than usual we'll finish for the day. I earlier asked the counsel for the Prosecution whether there was any indication that you would not be available after the weekend because this Chamber is not sitting on Friday, and therefore we will adjourn until Monday. Could we see you back Monday morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd prefer tomorrow, if possible; if not, I suppose I'll just have to accept what you're suggesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that would be a possibility to sit tomorrow, we certainly would have done that and this Chamber is always very concerned about witnesses being able to return before the weekend. Unfortunately we can't do it. So it's very much appreciated that you finally then accept that you have to stay until Monday. That's not what the Chamber would have preferred, but unfortunately there's no other solution for that. May I instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony, the testimony you have already given or still -- are still about to give. We'd like then to see you back Monday, the 2nd of July, 9.00 in the morning, in this same courtroom. Madam Usher, would you escort Mr. Bajcetic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, what is the message?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we would then on Monday start to hear the next witness in line? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would take us until?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Through the end of Tuesday, we believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And then beginning on Wednesday we will take the examination-in-chief of the following witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that's an expert witness, and then the -- the suggestion -- at least the proposal made by Mr. Emmerson was that he would not cross-examine that witness but that we would then continue -- well, as a matter of fact, he proposed two things. The first proposal was to delay the expert witnesses, both, and the subsidiary proposal was that both these expert witnesses would give their testimony in chief and be recalled for cross-examination at a later stage. These were the two proposals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. And, Your Honour, given the fact that the witness we're proposing for Wednesday, the estimate for his direct

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: witness -- that witness's direct will take up the three sessions of Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then what -- and that's of course now the issue, what would you then suggest to do on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I stand corrected, just reading on. There's a proposal -- may I have one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I assist? Does Your Honours have a copy of the e-mail yet? It's arrived on our screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now I have received it. 11 minutes past --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The proposal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- let me first read it so that we ... I think the estimates for time are not the issue; the issue is whether the Defence is ready to cross-examine the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do the following. The Chamber is not sitting tomorrow, but the Chamber will be in communication with the parties tomorrow to see how to proceed next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think, if I may say so, Monday, as suggested by Mr. Re, is entirely unobjectionable, it's the completion of the evidence of this witness, followed by the evidence in chief of the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tuesday we will, of course, be in a position to cross-examine that witness on Tuesday, he not being a forensic expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And my strong expectation is that he will take most of Tuesday, but not necessarily the third session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and there might be some argument as to exclusion of part of his evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anyhow, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then the following witness, that is to say -- I don't think there is any application for protective measures in respect of either of the pathologists, so that is to say Dr. Dusan Dunjic is suggested to be slotted in on Tuesday afternoon, but we would need the whole of Wednesday for the evidence in chief of Professor Aleksandric. Now, the short answer is, to Mr. Re's question, my own view is that is trying to squeeze a quart into a pint, as we say, pot; in other words, we will not reach Professor Dunjic or Dr. Dunjic on Tuesday afternoon in sufficient time to complete his evidence in chief. And given the need to ensure that Professor Aleksandric's evidence in chief can be heard, then, if we simply removed Dr. Dunjic from the equation that would provide a perfectly sensible running list for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and then Thursday I think the suggestion is that it be used as much as possible for tidying up all the outstanding procedural matters, because in any event I shan't be here on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would definitely concur with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would concur with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Most definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Harvey, would you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And we've spent some time trying to chart out the examinations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not only a question of timing, it's also a question of tactical advantages of not cross-examining one witness before the other one gives his examination-in-chief. I mean, it's more complex than it's just not a matter of scheduling. The Chamber therefore would like to thoroughly consider the matter, might be in touch with the parties tomorrow if need be, and then we will consider how to proceed next week. Mr. Kearney, if that is -- then -- yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That's completely appropriate for the Prosecution, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, you started a sentence with "Mr. Harvey would you," and the answer is yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey, I -- half a word in our communications does... We adjourn until Monday, 2nd of July, 9.00 in the morning, this same courtroom.
